result.title: Governance-State Corruption in Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents: A Cross-Model Stress Test
result.summary: An LLM agent can retrieve a memory correctly yet use it incorrectly after its validity state changes. We study governance-state corruption: faults that alter which retained records enter model-visible context while stored content and tasks remain fixed. Across six providers, 731 benchmark-grounded bases yield 2,080 matched fault pairs. In offline control-plane checks, corruption changes the operative projection in 96.25% of pairs, while oracle-backed enforcement restores it in 100%. For downstream evaluation, a deterministically selected, non-probability LongMemEval/Memora panel resolves 298 of 300 matched triplets (238 distinct bases). Clean-minus-corrupted contrasts are 40.54 percentage points in LongMemEval binary correctness (95% base-cluster interval [30.32, 50.71]) and 30.60 points in rescaled Memora FAMA ([23.31, 37.69]); both sources also show recovery. OAKS Novel native option parity holds for all 6,714 resolved outputs. Full-cohort frozen-scorer corruption/recovery effects (-27.55/+27.51 points) remain descriptive proxies, not validated native semantic population effects. These bounded findings motivate evaluating memory control-state integrity alongside retrieval accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 LLM agent 长期记忆中的「治理状态损坏」：内容与任务不变、仅哪些记录进入模型可见上下文的有效性状态被改变，据此在六家提供商、2,080 组配对故障上做压力测试，并在 LongMemEval/Memora 上测干净-受损差异与恢复。
AI.relevance_reason: 其配对故障注入与「干净减受损」对比框架可能可供核查，用于检验 LVR 中视觉证据是否真正进入推理并被使用，与证据筛选和状态治理线索相关；但对象是文本记忆，迁移需较多核查。
